name: Bolivia
sources: GDP $4.87bn and 7.13m people (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD and SP.POP.TOTL, 1990; exact prints $4.868bn and 7,130,142) - the smallest economy in this region's roster. The census of 3 June 1992 counted 6,420,792, which is the figure most Bolivian sources of the period use; the World Bank series carries the higher revised estimate and it is the one entered, for consistency with the rest of the roster.

Inflation 17.1% (INE annual average for 1990). This is the single most impressive number in the file: Bolivian inflation had run at 11,750% in 1985, and Decree 21060 of 29 August 1985 — the New Economic Policy — killed it in weeks. Bolivia enters 1990 as the region's stabilisation success and its poorest state at the same time. interest_rate 22% is the boliviano lending benchmark; roughly 80% of deposits were held in dollars, so the rate that binds is really the US one.
Tax take 12% of GDP after the 1986 tax reform rebuilt collection from nothing. Gross fixed capital formation about 12.5% of GDP, split 6% public and 7% private.

Debt 0.85: external debt about $4.3bn at end-1990 (World Bank), near 88% of GDP, despite the 1988 buy-back that retired commercial debt at eleven cents on the dollar. Bolivia is one of the original HIPC cases.

Oil 0.022 mbd: YPFB produced about 22,000 bbl/d of crude and condensate. The real hydrocarbon story is natural gas piped to Argentina under the 1972 contract, which is most of export earnings and is not a field this schema carries.

Defence 2.4% of GDP, strength 3. Stability 42: Bolivia had had a constitutional government since 1982 after decades of coups, but the tin price collapse of October 1985 had closed COMIBOL's mines and put 23,000 miners out of work, and coca eradication under US pressure — Operation Blast Furnace in 1986, the Annual Bilateral Agreements from 1987 — was a permanent confrontation with the Chapare growers' unions.

Separatism 0.10: not secession but the indigenous and regional question that produces the March for Territory and Dignity from Beni to La Paz in August 1990, and the Santa Cruz autonomy movement later.

pop_growth_1990 = 2.1352%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series BOL (Bolivia): 6,281,868 in 1984 to 6,981,766 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

reserves_bn = 0.563 ($bn). Total reserves including gold, BOL, 1989: US$563347083.00 (World Bank World Development Indicators series FI.RES.TOTL.CD, 'Total reserves (includes gold, current US$)', retrieved from the World Bank API on 2026-09-02; indicator lastupdated 2026-07-13). THE 1989 OBSERVATION AND NOT THE 1990 ONE: a reserve is a stock, and the stock on the morning of the 1 January 1990 start date is the end-1989 figure - the same reasoning pop_growth_1990 above gives for ending its window on 31 December 1989. LIMIT STATED: this series is official reserve assets. Sovereign wealth fund balances are not in it and none has been added, because no audited 1990 balance could be sourced for any of them; where that materially understates a state's usable stock it is reported rather than estimated (iron rule 4).

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

DATA-KEYED TAIL NATION. This nation is outside the 29 authored majors, so nothing here was authored technology by technology: a grant is made only where one of two named published global series supports it, and nothing is modelled, estimated or interpolated. A short list, or an empty one, is the correct outcome of that rule and not a gap in the work.

Data-keyed tail nation: not one of the 29 authored majors. Only the two series named in ruling 3 were consulted - WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 1990 and World Bank IT.CEL.SETS. Nothing was modelled, estimated or interpolated, and no other evidence was admitted. ISO3 key used for both series: BOL.
AUTHORED, AND THE ANSWER IS NOTHING. Both named series were checked and both refused this nation; the empty grant list is a finding, not an absence of work.

The other 46 grantable 1990 technologies are BLANK for this nation by design, not by oversight: the 17 sovereignty-side entries are unreachable by any use-in-operation series, and no published global series was named that keys the remaining 29 use-side entries.
